exposure: Paternal age at conception (≤30 years, 31-40 years, >40 years)
cohort: 16,268 patients who underwent IVF or ICSI using autologous sperm and donated oocytes at Spanish IVIRMA clinics between January 2008 and March 2020
finding: Advanced paternal age (31-40 years and >40 years) was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery and longer pregnancies compared to fathers ≤30 years old, but other medically relevant obstetrical and perinatal outcomes were comparable between groups.
mod_finding: Fathers aged 31-40 and >40 years old were associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery compared to fathers ≤30 years old.
